# Hard-to-vary report

## 1. The question, frozen

The title and opening centralize one question, so I froze that one: *what were the diagnostic and therapeutic trajectories of three patients with SSc-ILD who developed lung cancer at a tertiary, academic, safety-net centre, and what real-world considerations arise for evaluating and managing such patients?* Range: three patients, one centre, 2019–2023. Kind of question: mainly **backward** — what can we tell from what we see — plus a small **forward** claim (what produces the raised risk) and a **design** claim (what should be done). The paper also answers a bigger question about SSc-ILD risk in general; that answer is borrowed and is marked as such below.

## 2. The explanation in parts

P1 "SSc-ILD patients are at increased risk for lung cancer" (four-fold). P2 "abnormal lung parenchyma complicates screening and evaluation of nodules." P3 "longitudinal imaging review and PET/CT were critical." P4 "chronic inflammation, fibrosis-related architectural distortion, and immune dysregulation." P5 "smoking may not be the sole determinant." P6 "safety-net settings … social determinants of health impacting follow-up." P7 "multidisciplinary care … allowed for efficient diagnostic evaluation." P8 mycophenolate plus chemotherapy act on overlapping pathways and worsen marrow suppression. P9 "tocilizumab … may offer a more targeted alternative." P10 "nintedanib … is not an immunosuppressant and might itself be active against non-small cell lung cancer." P11 "interrupting therapy may come at the cost of worsening ILD." P12 "future research … is needed."

## 3. Part by part

| Part | Mark | Why |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | **Borrowed** | Rests on the epidemiology it cites, not on these three cases. The four-fold figure is a comparison across populations, never tested here. |
| P2 | **Held** (by case 1) | Case 1's first transthoracic biopsy was non-diagnostic and only resection settled it. But the sentence "Most of the patients described in our series had initial negative biopsies" is **not held by its own record**: one of three. Put the biopsy log beside that sentence. |
| P3 | **Two routes** | In case 1, interval growth on CT and PET avidity each independently pushed the surgical referral; either alone would have done it. In cases 2 and 3 PET did staging, not detection. So "PET was critical" is loose where "something beyond the plain CT read" is what is held. |
| P4 | **Loose as used here** | As a general claim it is borrowed. Used to explain *why these three*, it is a bin with no gauge: any cancer in any SSc-ILD patient fits inflammation, or fibrosis, or immune dysregulation. Name a reading that would show the bin swallowing a job. |
| P5 | **Held**, narrowly | A never-smoker with lung cancer does rule out "smoking is necessary." The stronger reading — smoking is not the main driver — is not held by one case. |
| P6 | **Idle** | No case attributes a delay to it. Remove it and nothing in the three trajectories changes. |
| P7 | **Held if** | Held only by the job "co-management sped evaluation," which was never contrasted. Trial: time from first abnormal scan to diagnosis, co-managed versus not. |
| P8 | **Borrowed**, with a gauge | The mechanism comes from other work, but it is the most testable part here: blood counts are the gauge, and they exist in these charts. |
| P9 | **Loose** | The authors say evidence is thin; a near neighbour (another targeted agent) would read the same. |
| P10 | **Half held, half borrowed** | "Not an immunosuppressant" follows from what the drug does. "Might be active against NSCLC" rests on other work. |
| P11 | **Held if** | The named cause does not set the amount. Pauses ran one year, four months, and three years before progression — no single interval follows from "we paused it." The doubtful job is that the pause, and not the disease's own course, did the worsening. |
| P12 | **Fixed** | A genre convention. It is also the honest signal that the change list is empty. |

## 4. Whole-explanation checks

**Flip.** Would any sentence read differently if the three patients had *not* developed cancer? Vigilance, PET, multidisciplinary care and pause-then-resume would all read the same. If ILD had stayed stable through a pause, nothing written here says what would have been concluded instead.

**Direction.** The paper runs backward from three found cancers to a claim about what produces risk. That is fine for "what can we tell," not for "what produces it." There is no denominator: how many SSc-ILD patients this clinic follows, how many nodules it watches, how many turned out benign.

**Answer in the starting points.** "Chronic inflammation, fibrosis, immune dysregulation" is the conclusion ("cancer happens") placed at the start under three names. It fixes no interval, no dose, no prediction.

**Jobs I added.** The "did not happen" jobs: SSc-ILD patients with nodules that were benign, and patients who held immunosuppression and did not progress. The paper does not do these, and says so.

**Pairs that pull.** Heightened suspicion and lower biopsy thresholds pull against procedural risk in fibrotic lung; holding immunosuppression for cancer control pulls against ILD progression. Both tensions are named, neither is resolved to a line. The line is drawn per patient, afterwards.

**Catch-alls.** P4 and P6 are bins with no gauges.

**Rivals.** "The ILD progressed because SSc-ILD progresses, not because of the pause" is not separated off. Nor is "these cancers were caught because this clinic scans often." Nothing on the change list tells them apart.

**Where parts came from.** Nearly everything is borrowed from epidemiology and mechanism papers, or asserted (multidisciplinary care, safety net). One internal claim (P2's "most") is fitted to a memory rather than to the record.

## 5. What would make it harder to vary

Two pulls. First, the same clinic's denominator: patients under surveillance in the window, nodules followed, resections that came back benign. Second, a table of every immunosuppression pause in the clinic — dates held, dates of ILD progression, and the patients who did not progress — with the authors writing beforehand what pattern would count against P11.

## 6. What this does not show

Hard to vary is not true. Passing would not prove the risk claims or the management advice. Failing says nothing about whether pausing immunosuppression is safe — only that this paper does not hold that part in place.

## 7. One next step

Pull the denominator and the benign-nodule count from the same clinic and window, and write down, before looking, which result would count against the heightened-suspicion recommendation.

P8 Mycophenolate/chemo pathway: borrowed (mechanism from other literature: overlapping action on dividing cells). The mechanistic part is plausible and not tested here; but it is concrete — a poke exists (blood counts). Mark borrowed, with a gauge: blood counts. Actually it's a mechanism claim with a clear observable (cytopenias), so it's the least loose — held if tested. Mark borrowed and say the gauge exists.
P9 Tocilizumab: loose — the authors themselves say little evidence; nearly any targeted agent could be swapped in. Mark loose, name a replacement (abatacept/rituximab etc.) — hmm, in SSc-ILD, tocilizumab approved; swap for another targeted biologic. Fine.
P10 Nintedanib: borrowed (anti-tumour activity claim rests on other work); the "not an immunosuppressant" half is a rule/definition thing — held (by its mechanism), the "may be active against NSCLC" is borrowed.
P11 Interrupting immunosuppression worsens ILD: this is the central therapeutic claim. Parts held by three cases, but the intervals are all different: paused 1 year (case 1), 4 months (case 2), 3 years (case 3) before progression. Nothing in the claim fixes these timings, so what holds the timing? Mark loose/held if: the cause named doesn't set the amount. Poke: a patient who holds immunosuppression and doesn't progress; or one who continues immunosuppression and progresses anyway (case 1 progressed... no). Also flip: for case 3, resumed after 3 years for ILD progression — could the same sentence have been written if immunosuppression had been held throughout? Yes; it's written as a sequence, not a contrast. And is ILD progression the natural course of SSc-ILD regardless? That rival is not ruled out. Mark: held if (doubtful job: that holding immunosuppression is what worsened the ILD rather than the disease's own course; the test: ILD progression in patients who stayed on therapy, and timing comparisons).
P12 Future research: idle or free — conventional; but "future research needed" is the honest statement of the change list's emptiness. Mark fixed/free: say plainly it's the standard closing; it is not a finding. I'd mark it idle (can be removed with no loss from the explanation) — or better "fixed" (a genre requirement). I'll say fixed (a convention of the genre) — allowed to be loose.

Whole-explanation checks:
- Flip: would the paper read any differently if the three patients had not developed cancer? The parts that do the work (vigilance, multidisciplinary care, hold-then-resume immunosuppression) would read the same. Also: flip on immunosuppression outcome — if ILD had not progressed, would the paper have concluded the opposite (holding is fine)? Nothing in the paper says what would have counted against.
- Direction: the paper runs backward from three diagnosed cases to the claim that SSc-ILD raises risk. Backward is fine for "what can we tell", not for "what produces it". No denominators: how many SSc-ILD patients are followed at BMC, how many nodules turned out benign. That's the missing change list — nothing that "could have mattered" is on it.
- Answer hidden in starting points: "chronic inflammation, fibrosis, immune dysregulation" — a bin where the conclusion ("cancer happens") is present under a new name. In a matter of fact if the mechanisms cause cancer, the bin is fine; the problem is the bin sets no interval, no dose, no prediction.
- Jobs: added by me — the "did not happen" job (SSc-ILD patients with nodules that were benign; SSc-ILD patients who kept immunosuppression and did not progress). The paper does not do these.
- Pairs that pull: heightened suspicion / lower thresholds for biopsy vs procedural risk in fibrotic lung; hold immunosuppression for cancer control vs ILD progression. The paper names both tensions but does not say which gives way at which point. So the line is drawn per-patient, retrospectively.

That would hold or break the heightened-suspicion claim. (2) a table of every immunosuppression pause in the clinic with dates held and dates of ILD progression (and the ones that did not progress), with the authors writing down beforehand what pattern would count against.
